plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This ensures I never overpay and capture surplus whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid. With a private value of $6, deviating (bidding higher or lower) only risks negative profit or lost opportunity. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding truthfully (equal to my private value) is the dominant strategy. Since I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot round, the optimal approach is to bid exactly my value of $40, ensuring I maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while bidding below reduces your chance of winning without any benefit. With a value of $28, I should bid exactly $28 to maximize expected profit.
